text:
alex: Heads up — canary rollout for release/1763 shows a regression on 1-shot text-gen p95. ~2.3x latency increase compared to last stable. Not huge traffic but reproducible in lab.

maria: ack. is this on the dedicated pool or hosted canary?

alex: dedicated-small pool we use for canaries. Replayed the same prompt set locally and saw same.

jonathan: CI perf job also failed earlier: `perf/inference/latency-stable` threshold exceeded. ci-bot posted stack there.

ci-bot: [CI] perf/inference/latency-stable — failed — p95 increased by 128% vs baseline. Build: ci/1763-merge. Link: https://ci.redwood/1763/build/2045

emma: any obvious churn in runtime lately? kernel-selection or batching heuristics changes?

alex: last merges that touched runtime: PR #3421 (kernel selector heuristics), PR #3438 (kvcache eviction refactor), and a small batching tweak in #3440.

maria: can we bisect quickly across those? Start with reverting batching tweak locally and replay?

samir: I ran a quick bisect yesterday: disabling the kernel-selector change dropped p95 back ~35%. KV cache refactor also moved the needle but less. Batching tweak alone had negligible effect.

jonathan: interesting — kernel-selector change was trying to prefer fused kernels for medium sequence lengths. Could be picking a slower kernel for the canary workload distribution.

alex: attaching a minimal repro and profiler snapshot. Repro command: 
```
./run_repro --model redwood-v1 --seq 512 --batch-dist 90/10 --requests 1000
```
Profiler extract (short): 
```
kernel_select_time: 12.4ms -> now 34.9ms per step
attention_kernel_fused: chosen 68% -> previous 12%
```

maria: thanks. that's a big visible increase in kernel select overhead. If the selector is doing more heavy evaluation per request, that explains the regression. Did we increase cost model complexity?

samir: PR #3421 replaced a constant-time heuristic with a small dynamic cost model using microbenchmarks at startup to pick kernels. Looks like the microbenchmark is biased by cache-warm sequences and is choosing a kernel that's worse for the live request distribution.

jonathan: ok. quick mitigation: fall back to the previous heuristic when sampled throughput/latency deviates by >10% from microbenchmark predictions. Could patch as hotfix.

alex: I pushed a revert of the kernel selector portion to the canary branch and restarted canary. deploy-bot shows rollout.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary/dedicated-small -> build ci/1763-hotfix-3470. Canaries: 3/3 started.

ci-bot: [CI] perf/inference/latency-stable — rerun — passed (p95 within threshold).

maria: good. we should still fix the selector but make microbenchmarks reflect actual distribution (or use a cheaper online sampling method).

emma: for post-release retro: propose adding a targeted perf test that mixes seq lengths and cache-hit ratios to catch this kernel-selection regression earlier. Current perf test only uses seq=256 fixed.

jonathan: +1. also add a test that exercises kvcache eviction patterns — PR #3438 changed LRU behavior and we saw small regression there too under high-concurrency evictions. It was masked by kernel change.

samir: notes from profiling: KV cache eviction spike causes spiky GC-style pauses in allocator which amplify p95. Sample snippet from trace:
```
EVICT_START 12:03:45.112
free_block_scan 12.03ms
reclaim_write_lock 5.2ms
KV_UPDATE lag spike 18.7ms
```

emma: action items I captured: 
- tighten perf CI: add mixed-workload benchmark (seq 64/256/512 mix) and kvcache-eviction scenario.
- tune thresholds per workload (don't use one-size-fits-all p95).
- make kernel-selector opt-in until cost model has better sampling.
- add a flaky-test tracker for perf tests that rerun 3x before marking failure.

alex: +1. also let's add logging of kernel decision path in verbose mode so when CI fails we can capture the chosen kernel and microbenchmark samples. Make sure logs are redacted for customers.

maria: I'll draft a perf-test spec doc and put it in eng-runtime/perf-tests. Will include sample configs and thresholds.

jonathan: one more thought — automatic canary rollback on >20% deviation would've caught this earlier. We have the infra but thresholds are wide. Tighten canary rollback rules for runtime patches.

samir: created quick RFC: https://go.redwood/rfcs/runtime-kernel-selector-3475 (proposal: revert cost-model default, add online sampling, and perf test).

alex: thanks everyone. Happy path: revert landed to canary, perf CI green, creating a follow-up ticket to reintroduce kernel selector behind a flag with better sampling.

ci-bot: Created issue perf/1763-kernel-selector-followup #521.

emma: Let's sync tomorrow 10am for retro and assign owners.

alex: pinging @maria @jonathan to prepare short notes. :thumbsup:

maria: on it.
